page: Microsoft Azure M32ms is a memory-optimized server belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with an Intel Xeon 8280M processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs and 16 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The server features a massive memory allocation of 875.0 GB, translating to 27.34 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, it includes 1049 GB of local storage and is Premium Storage capable, while containing no GPU hardware.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile characterized by a tradeoff between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression tests falling into the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, achieve average performance in the middle 50% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with database and Redis SET operations, also consistently perform at average levels, though the Passmark memory score is positioned in the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-threaded performance, the M32ms is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that demand extreme memory capacity rather than raw CPU speed. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive enterprise applications, large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and data processing tasks that can leverage its 875.0 GB RAM footprint.
